verdict: V2 fixes HPIO-001/002/004/005 and corrects HPIO-007. Live-object root pinning works under the explicit stable-root TCB. Two new local hardening findings remain, and HPIO-003 plus root/actual-T16 integration remain external launch conditions. P0 is not launch-admissible.

v1_finding_disposition.evidence: admit_intent validates exact current canonical bytes, publishes a content-addressed three-file store before the admission record (317-337,549-629), and select_final_method reads the selected admitted store rather than active source (368-408). Across separate Python interpreters, candidate A remained selectable after candidate B and a final_refit intent; the private copy matched A while active source differed. Stored-byte tamper returned STATE_CORRUPT.

_snapshot_from_fd decrements remaining closure capacity and gives each descriptor the smaller file/remaining cap (530-547). Independent read spy saw [8] only for 8+8+8 bytes under file cap 10 and closure cap 15, then LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

DevResultReceipt remains a trusted-root input shape; _permitted_receipt_tuples checks only type/hash shapes (674-683). An arbitrary well-shaped tuple was still accepted. This is consistent with the code/report boundary, but no actual bridge receipt opening/provenance was tested.

Final identity now derives inside the transaction from stored selection closure/code/receipt/task/environment/protocol plus phase/config/manifests (238-253,424-452); different stored selections yielded different identities. A post-write state selection tamper was rejected after restart.

_validate_snapshot_shape bounds bytes and recomputes all file and closure hashes (647-672); forged fields/bytes returned INVALID_VALUE. Admission additionally requires equality with a freshly opened canonical snapshot (317-325).

Roots are canonicalized and device/inode-pinned at construction (258-263,936-959,1088-1110). Same live object rejected source/state path replacement. A new interpreter after wholesale state-root replacement re-anchored the new directory and admitted the same closure, so process-restart safety still requires the documented stable trusted root/ancestor/mount deployment condition.
The local test is renamed without T16 attribution (test_trusted_io.py:471-479), and trusted-io-report/v2 explicitly leaves actual extension/root T16 evidence open.

new_findings.title: Reloaded final_lock does not cross-check duplicated config/manifest fields against final_refit
new_findings.evidence: lock_final_artifact copies execution_config_sha256, outer_training_manifest_sha256, and hidden_features_manifest_sha256 from the refit record (510-512). _read_state cross-checks lock selection, execution identity, run, task, environment, and protocol (906-923) but omits those three duplicated fields. After locking, replacing final_lock.execution_config_sha256 with another valid SHA-256 and reloading returned the tampered value as ACCEPTED.
new_findings.impact: The durable FinalArtifactLock can expose a config/manifest value inconsistent with the execution identity and final-refit record. This weakens canonical provenance even though hostile state-root writers remain outside the TCB.
new_findings.required_fix: In _read_state, require the lock's execution_config_sha256, outer_training_manifest_sha256, and hidden_features_manifest_sha256 to equal the final_refit_admission record. Add a restart regression for each duplicated field.

new_findings.title: Failed snapshot publication leaves unaccounted private-store directories
new_findings.evidence: _store_snapshot creates a random temporary directory (571-586) but has no exception cleanup. A forced mid-store failure left one .snapshot-* directory after successful later recovery. Also, admit_intent stores/renames the full snapshot before _write_state checks max_state_bytes (334-336,926-931). With max_state_bytes=400, four distinct snapshots were stored while only two admissions fit; the other calls returned LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
new_findings.impact: max_state_bytes does not bound accumulated snapshot-store bytes, and handled write failures can leave garbage. The root's frozen attempt limit may bound the production exposure, but that bound is external and must not be inferred from this module.
new_findings.required_fix: Clean a known private temporary directory on handled pre-rename failure. Preflight the next canonical state encoding before storing, or add/enforce an explicit total snapshot count/byte cap derived from the frozen attempt budget. Define how valid post-rename/pre-state crash orphans are reconciled without automatic external-run retry.

confirmed_local_controls: Twenty-three authored tests reproduced from exact copied bytes.
Historical selection uses private stored bytes and survives a fresh interpreter, changed active candidate, and final_refit intent.
Tampered private closure bytes and selection-bound execution identity fail closed after reload.
A durable store created before a handled state-publication failure is verified/reused on the next interpreter and produces one PENDING admission.
Aggregate closure capacity stops the next descriptor before os.read; per-file descriptor checks remain.
Forged Snapshot carrier fields/bytes fail INVALID_VALUE.
Typed final phase and local PENDING/BOUND process fences from T09/T14 remain covered by the authored suite.
T16 is not claimed by the local snapshot test.
external_launch_conditions: HPIO-003: the actual root bridge must open the real eligible dev receipt at the expected trusted root, derive receipt/closure/code, and construct DevResultReceipt internally; controller/self-attested fields are not authority.
The actual final artifact hash/binding must likewise come from the root-owned sealed artifact/receipt path; this module only validates the trusted input shape.

Stable canonical source/state roots and ancestors must be protected across process restarts. Live device/inode pinning cannot detect a wholesale trusted-root replacement before a new process anchors it.
Actual T16 extension pre/post hash, size, mtime upper bound, loaded absolute path, prompt/image/argv/tool-census evidence remains outside these files.
ORX lifecycle/reconciliation, fixed argv/image, Docker/custody, generated code, scorer, raw data, provider/auth, and scientific run evidence remain untested here.
